hyps.why: Replacing a removed edge with a 3x3 conv adds far more than replacing an existing parametric or skip op.
Adding a conv where the edge was dead gives a larger gain than swapping one op for another.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with skip loses learnable capacity, unlike replacing none or pooling.
Without the direct 0->3 path, the conv on 2->3 matters more because the cell relies on it.
With edge 1 removed, edge 0 carries most of the input signal, so a stronger op there matters more.
When edge 0 is dead, edge 1 is the only route from the input to the deeper nodes.
Reviving a dead edge with a conv gives a larger gain than replacing another op.
Replacing a conv with pooling is a large loss, whereas replacing none with pooling is neutral or a gain.
With no direct skip path, the conv on 1->3 contributes more to the output.
Adding a residual path where the edge was removed helps more than replacing an existing op with skip.
